findings.message: reads sensitive system or credential files
findings.remediation: Never read system files, credential stores, or environment files from plugins.
findings.impact: Reading system credential files exposes SSH private keys, AWS credentials, and Docker tokens.
findings.attack_vector: File path matches /etc/passwd, ~/.ssh/id_rsa, ~/.aws/credentials — secrets are read into memory.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: writes to system directories or boot locations
findings.remediation: Restrict file writes to user-owned directories with explicit approval.
findings.impact: System startup and installation directories are sensitive destinations for persistent modification.
findings.attack_vector: Source references a boot or system directory; this low lead does not by itself prove mutation or privilege.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.remediation: Require explicit user approval for any shell profile modification.
findings.impact: Shell startup files can execute added commands in future terminal sessions.
findings.attack_vector: Source references a shell rc file; this low lead does not by itself prove a write occurs.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
